answer: Each challenge is instantiated only after a specified future drand quicknet pulse, whose threshold-BLS signature makes the beacon output publicly verifiable and unpredictable before release. A participant commits to its response, then reveals it for verification against the pulse-derived task; this blocks advance computation and makes offline sybil farming costly, though it cannot by itself prove one human per identity. A jetty, lotus, and wharf may label distinct task domains, not bypass the shared randomness.
